scope.summary: Implement canonical-space skinning weight re-projection at extremes per Section 13.18 (BK-18.2, TAI-BK-062), closing REQ-019: weights are defined once in canonical (neutral) space and re-projected onto the deformed surface as regions grow, so giant breasts, glutes, and bellies keep clean deformation at 300% ranges — deterministic and covered by the pose-range matrix.
acceptance_criteria: reproject_weights(canonical_weights, neutral_mesh, deformed_mesh) maps canonical-space influences onto the channel-deformed surface (surface-relative mapping, not raw vertex copy); output stays normalized with the influence cap respected.
Determinism: identical inputs produce bit-identical re-projected weights across runs.

Extreme-region proof: at breast_volume 3.0, posing the breast_l chain deforms the enlarged breast without collapse or shear versus the un-re-projected control (quantified vertex-quality comparison, the giant-breast clean-deformation assertion; same fixture pattern for glute_volume max).

Re-projection triggers mechanically from the channel-change pipeline when a region's cumulative deformation passes a documented threshold; below threshold canonical weights pass through unchanged (no needless churn).
Canonical weights remain the stored authority — re-projected weights are derived state, never written back over the canonical artifact (negative test).
scope.risk_if_missed: Fixed neutral-space weights are why Daz bodies with huge breasts/glutes deform like sacks under pose; without re-projection the operator's extreme-volume archetypes pass static validation and then break in every posed shot — the worst possible failure timing.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/solver scope: behavior is observable via TraceProjection, typed TAILOR_BODY_* receipts, and the 13.12 capture APIs; operator/model GUI exposure rides the BodyKit panes (13.27) and is validated there.

target_entries: Tailor UserManual > BodyKit skeleton and rigging

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Pure computation or schema-only behavior has no independent lifecycle event; its owning run records inputs, outputs, diagnostics, and receipts.
This MT emits typed diagnostics through its owning command or job and inherits retention, health, and projection behavior from the shared diagnostics substrate.
This bounded in-process computation has no application or child-process watch surface.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.

required_changes_before_execution: Validate feathered support, partition weights, declared compensation, and skeletal propagation instead of hard zero boundaries.
Consume the signed technical refinement, canonical command/surface registries, classified HBR tiers, and task-oriented UserManual contract before execution.

requirements: Resolve Principal, AuthenticatedSession and AccessSpace before every resource read or mutation.
Use PostgreSQL RLS/FORCE RLS and ResourceBroker-backed artifact/file handles; UI filtering is never the security boundary.
Derived resources preserve the intersection of source access scopes and must not leak existence through counts, search, previews, logs, traces, caches, diagnostics, exports or model context.
